chapter: Playing fast, best gigs and the future
title: Best gig: Ray Barretto at Carnegie Hall
summary: His best gig was playing his own tunes with Ray Barretto at Carnegie Hall; every gig is a challenge.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Here’s a question that sometimes is hard to answer, but do you have a best gig and a worst gig that stick in your mind?

Well the best gig is a hard one because I think the best gig was probably, just for like the prestige of it or the feeling, was when I played with Ray Baretto and we played the JC Jazz Festival at Carnegie Hall and we were playing my tunes in Carnegie Hall. That was, for a musician, jazz or otherwise, it doesn’t get much better than that, and being paid well. You know and the worst gigs, you know how that goes, there was some real bad ones but I don’t want to go there.

I know, most people don’t. Sometimes it’s not even the music it’s like getting home from the gig or this happened. Even coming here today you had some trouble, but that doesn’t make it your worst gig. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-

But you know the thing with me is that like I try to — whether I’m at Carnegie Hall and some band room in Vancouver, Connecticut giving a clinic to some middle school kids, I really try to go with the same attitude. Just play from your heart and try to play as best as you can and try to be a good trumpet player, and try to just play standard licks or whatever, you know, and that, so to me every gig is a challenge. It really is a challenge.

That’s a pretty good statement right there. I guess we could wrap up and get you to your next engagement. But I do think it’s neat that you said that one of your best things ever was hearing your own music. There’s something really special about that.

That was, if I had to pick one night in particular, that was, you know I’ve had many great experiences in music, you know, being a sideman with great singers or being on TV and stuff like that. You know stuff like that is exciting. But that hall like that, there is something about Carnegie Hall, there really is. I played in many great halls all over the world, and it’s really something special acoustically, you know, acoustically. It’s really incredible. Something happens there. There’s just a certain sound, the sound just gets carried like it’s beautiful.
